scope: Agenda and staff reports reviewed, with targeted comparisons of the Axon quote, budget adjustment form and Stewart Park bid documents. All 87 bookmarked supporting documents are inventoried; this is not a substantive review of every page. The City's separate HTML agenda inventory could not be verified.

items.title: Approval of October 20 minutes
items.summary: Consider the October 20, 2026 Council minutes. These are supplied for approval on November 17; their presence in the packet does not establish that Council has adopted them.

items.title: October City Attorney invoices
items.summary: Consider October 2026 City Attorney invoices. The SBEMP cover letter reports $109,307.09 due for professional services through October 31.
items.funding: Reported invoice amount, not proof of payment.

items.title: Investment policy update
items.summary: Approve Chandler Asset Management's recommended investment-policy revisions and authorize implementation. Staff says the guidelines do not themselves authorize spending or require purchase of a security.

items.title: Sundance street improvement bond releases
items.summary: Record notices of completion and accept Sundance Starlight Avenue and Tracts 31469-7 and 31469-9 street improvements into the maintained system. Staff reports $802,130.06 in accepted asset value, with maintenance through Public Works.

items.title: Fairways sewer and Pinehurst monumentation bond releases
items.summary: Consider performance bond releases for Big Canyon and Ridge View sewer improvements and Pinehurst monumentation. Staff identifies $574,000 in sewer assets and Wastewater operating maintenance. Confirm the motion covers all improvements listed in the item.

items.title: Fairway Canyon sewer lift station bond release
items.summary: Record a notice of completion and accept the Tract 31462 sewer lift station improvements. Staff reports $1,833,048.68 in sewer assets, with maintenance through Wastewater.

items.title: Olivewood street performance bond release
items.summary: Record a notice of completion and accept Olivewood Tract 27971 street improvements. Staff reports $13,455 in accepted asset value and Public Works operating maintenance.

items.title: Olivewood sewer and street maintenance bond releases
items.summary: Accept Olivewood Tract 27971 sewer and Tract 27971-7 street improvements and release maintenance bonds after the one-year period. Staff reports sewer assets of $26,823.06 and street assets of $80,542.78.

items.title: Police vehicle network upgrade
items.summary: Authorize a $125,636.94 CDCE agreement and purchase order for 40 Cradlepoint R2155 routers, installation and four-year NetCloud service plans.
items.funding: Staff identifies existing FY2026–27 Information Technology Internal Service Fund funding, with no additional appropriation requested.

items.title: Axon cameras, licenses and bundled AI services
items.summary: Consider a $130,314.94 Axon addition for eight body-worn cameras and 12 Pro user licenses. The attached quote also includes AI Assistant, Draft One report writing, transcription, redaction and Fusus livestream licenses.
items.funding: Staff identifies the Police operating budget and future budget cycles. The quote spans January 2027–February 2031.

checks.title: Quote scope includes AI tools and a different payment date
checks.text: The staff report describes a four-year camera/license addition. The quote specifies 50 months, includes $40,512 for AI Assistant and Draft One, and lists transcription, redaction and Fusus licenses. Its June 1, 2028 payment date differs from July 2028 in the staff report; the total agrees. Clarify the authorized service scope, policy safeguards and controlling payment schedule.

items.title: Alcohol enforcement and education grant
items.summary: Accept a $22,000 ABC grant funded through the Office of Traffic Safety and authorize agreement 27-OTS102. Eligible personnel overtime, benefits and specified travel are reimbursable; staff identifies no required City match.

items.title: Temporary T-Mobile City Hall lease reinstatement
items.summary: Reinstate the existing City Hall communications-site lease through no later than May 22, 2027, while negotiating a successor lease and separately addressing the roof-damage claim. Either party may terminate with 60 days' notice. Staff reports current rent of $2,947.63 per month; the amendment does not establish a new rate or settle the damage claim.

items.title: Second readings of City committee ordinances
items.summary: Consider adoption of Public Works Advisory, Parks and Recreation, and Economic Development committee provisions, and amendments to the Financial and Audit Committee chapter. The proposals follow the October 20 first readings.

items.title: Short-term rental ordinance second reading
items.summary: Consider adoption of Chapter 5.21 covering licensing, operations, enforcement and transient occupancy tax requirements for short-term rentals. Community Development would administer the program; staff says fee and tax revenues cannot yet be determined.

items.title: First-quarter cash and investment report
items.summary: Receive and file cash and investment reports as of September 30, 2026. Receiving the reports does not itself authorize expenditures or adjust the budget.

items.title: First-quarter budget results and adjustment
items.summary: Receive and file first-quarter budget results and approve the accompanying budget adjustment. Staff reports General Fund spending of $15.2 million, about 19.3% of the $78.5 million budget; the recommended adjustment table totals $1,643,493.

checks.title: Adjustment descriptions need reconciliation
checks.text: The report's summary labels a $53,000 Planning increase as Weed Abatement, while the adjustment form describes Golden Triangle annexation professional services. The summary totals $1,643,493; staff says the changes stay within existing resources. Ask Finance to reconcile the descriptions and distinguish appropriation changes, transfers and coding corrections before treating the total as new spending.

items.title: October financial reports
items.summary: Receive and file governmental, proprietary and fiduciary fund receipts, disbursements and balances through October. Beginning balances are unaudited. Receiving the reports does not authorize expenditures or a budget adjustment.

checks.title: Attachment letters differ from the report list
checks.text: The report lists B as Proprietary and C as Fiduciary. The packet bookmarks instead label B as Fiduciary and C as Proprietary. Use the document contents and retained page references to identify the correct fund report.

items.title: Surplus declaration for part of APN 424-010-007
items.summary: Consider declaring a portion of City-owned parcel 424-010-007 surplus and authorizing availability notices. This starts a disposition process; the proposed declaration does not itself sell the property or establish sale proceeds.

items.title: Special counsel contract extensions
items.summary: Extend agreements with Burke, Williams & Sorensen and Liebert Cassidy Whitmore for as-needed specialized legal work. Staff lists hourly ranges of $205–$435 and $295–$485 respectively, with costs assigned to the fund related to the matter.

items.title: Proposed severe-weather local emergency declaration
items.summary: Consider a local emergency proclamation and emergency orders for anticipated severe-weather incidents. Staff describes expedited procurement and a basis for potential eligible cost reimbursement; no fixed expenditure amount or reimbursement award is established by this proposal.

items.title: $741,255.35 Vactor sewer cleaning truck
items.summary: Authorize a purchase order to Haaker Equipment Company for a Vactor 2115 Combo Sewer Cleaner through Sourcewell contract 021726-ELG.
items.funding: CIP WW27-01 has an $826,699 approved budget funded by Wastewater Repair and Replace funds. The requested purchase is $85,443.65 below that project budget; this difference is not a statement of uncommitted project funds.

items.title: Stewart Park Phase II construction bid package
items.summary: Approve Phase II plans and specifications and authorize advertisement for construction bids. Proposed amenities include a secondary playground, skate park work, basketball/pickleball courts, picnic shelters, a stage bandshell, paths, lighting and landscaping. This is bid authorization, not a construction contract award.
items.funding: Staff reports no fiscal impact from this recommended action and anticipates a 45-day advertisement period with bids in January 2027. The separate Phase I schedule identifies March 2027 completion with potential weather delays.

checks.title: Keep Phase I completion separate from Phase II bidding
checks.text: The March 2027 completion statement is in the Phase I progress update. Phase II is proposed for bid solicitation, with bids anticipated in January 2027. Do not present March 2027 as a confirmed completion date for the full park or Phase II. Attachment F is a one-page contract-drawings reference; the Phase II bid plan set is Attachment I, pages 1249–1313.
